children: Keyera shares fell Friday morning after the company lowered its guidance for the year due to pipeline disruptions and equipment issues at its Alberta processing facility.
Shares traded 4.7% lower at 55.75 Canadian dollars ($40.41).

The Calgary, Alberta-based energy infrastructure company late Thursday said it now expects realized margin at its marketing segment to be between C$320 million and C$350 million, down from a previous C$360 million to C$390 million.

The guidance drop stems from two distinct supply-chain and facility issues. The first is Enbridge's Line 5 pipeline, which has been shut down since Aug. 25 following an accidental third-party line strike in Wisconsin. Keyera estimates the disruption will reduce its marketing margin by roughly C$30 million.

The second is Keyera's Alberta EnviroFuels facility, which only just restarted production of iso-octane after a five-month outage. The company noted that the facility requires additional equipment replacements that will require it to operate at around 70% capacity through April 2027.
